Edge specification operators

Source: R/dsl.R
edge-operators.Rd

Infix operators used inside cgraph(), add_edges(), and remove_edges() to specify edges, e.g. A %-->% X + Y. Multiple edges fan out from (or into) a single marker with +: A %-->% X + Y means A --> X and A --> Y; chaining connects consecutive nodes pairwise, so X %-->% M %-->% Y means X --> M and M --> Y.

Usage

lhs %-->% rhs

lhs %<--% rhs

lhs %---% rhs

lhs %<->% rhs

lhs %o->% rhs

lhs %<-o% rhs

lhs %o--% rhs

lhs %--o% rhs

lhs %o-o% rhs

Arguments

lhs, rhs

Node name(s): a bare symbol, a string, or a +-combination or c() of either.

Value

Not meaningful on its own; see the Description.

Details

OperatorMeaning
%-->%directed, src --> dst
%<--%directed, dst --> src
%---%undirected
%<->%bidirected
%o->%partially directed, src o-> dst
%<-o%partially directed, dst o-> src
%o--%partially undirected, src o-- dst
%--o%partially undirected, dst o-- src
%o-o%partial (both ends circle)

These operators only make sense inside the ... of cgraph(), add_edges(), or remove_edges(), which capture their arguments unevaluated; they are not exported and are not meant to be called directly.

Examples

if (julia_ready()) {
  dag <- cgraph(A %-->% X + Y, X %-->% M %-->% Y)
  edges(dag)
}
#>   from to type
#> 1    A  X  -->
#> 2    A  Y  -->
#> 3    X  M  -->
#> 4    M  Y  -->
